targets.authors: Adams, G. S., Converse, B. A., Hales, A. H., & Klotz, L. E.
targets.title: People systematically overlook subtractive changes.
targets.evidence_quote: The study described here was a close replication, but also an extension of Experiments 2, 3 and 4 in Adams and colleagues (2021)’s study.
targets.outcome_quote: Unlike the original experiment, we found evidence that the cue affected (i.e., increased) the likelihood that participants would submit a list with at least one additive idea (OR = 2.52, 95% CI [1.45, 4.57], p < .001). As in the original experiment, we also found evidence that the cue increased the likelihood that participants would submit a list with at least one subtractive idea (OR = 2.52, 95% CI [1.73, 3.71], p < .001).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly contrast an additive cue effect with the original while confirming the subtractive cue effect. Statements that the central overlooking effect replicated concern that effect rather than an overall verdict covering the stated contrast.

reasoning: A completed preregistered new-sample replication with extensions. Exact v1 paper identity and author list verified against OSF/OpenAlex; the anonymous manuscript itself has no author byline. References included. Extensions do not create extra original targets.
